q: Name something that turned out to be Turing complete.
hint: Bonus points if nobody meant it to be.

answers.l: John Conway, 1970. People have built Life inside Life.
Redstone. Players have built working CPUs, slowly.
Discovered, not designed. Erwin Unruh’s 1994 program printed prime numbers as compiler errors.
LAMBDA, added in 2021, made plain formulas Turing complete. Microsoft said so itself.
HTML and CSS can run Rule 110, if a human keeps clicking.
In 2025, Dimitri Mitropoulos ran DOOM using only TypeScript’s type system.
Matthew Cook proved it universal in the 1990s. Wolfram Research’s legal action delayed publication until 2004.
Churchill, Biderman and Herrick, 2019. Deciding who wins a game can be undecidable.
Tom Wildenhain, SIGBOVIK 2017. A Turing machine built from animations and clicks.
Recursive common table expressions, from SQL:1999, did it.
Stephen Dolan, 2013: "mov is Turing-complete." Chris Domas then wrote a compiler that emits only movs.
Players have built computers out of water, minecarts and dwarves.
Its circuit network combinators are enough to build a computer.
Someone wrote an arbitrary-precision calculator in it, dc.sed. Someone else wrote Sokoban.
Recursive $(call) and $(eval) make it a programming language whether you like it or not.
Carlini and colleagues, 2015: printf with %n is Turing complete. "Control-Flow Bending."
Radu Grigore, 2016. Type-checking Java is therefore undecidable.
With UndecidableInstances on, instance resolution can compute anything.
Two simple rules on a grid. Shown universal in 2000.
Richard Kaye showed that infinite Minesweeper is Turing complete.
Bangert and colleagues, 2013: the MMU computes through page faults while no instruction runs.
Debug info’s expression bytecode is Turing complete. Oakley and Bratus used it for exploits in 2011.
Robert Berger, 1966: whether a tile set can cover the plane is undecidable.
Rewrite rules powerful enough to compute anything, readable by almost no one.

nope.regular expressions: Strictly weaker, in theory. Real engines with backreferences get weird, but no.
nope.regex: Strictly weaker, in theory. Real engines with backreferences get weird, but no.
nope.lambda calculus: Turing complete on purpose. We’re after the accidents.
nope.html: HTML alone, no. HTML plus CSS, maybe.

traps.q: Name the cellular automaton John Conway introduced in 1970.
Name the game whose redstone circuits players use to build working CPUs.
